content.comment_body: 1-When trying to control output Q1 in [product_name] at 192.168.0.2 via network output NQ2/192.168.0.2, the red operation indicator for Q1 in the simulation does not appear. 2-If the project includes the graphic symbol for Q1, then VB1064.0 shows 0.
If an output (such as Q1) is connected to logic on the input side in the diagram, it cannot be switched remotely. Bit V1064.0 simply mirrors the state of Q1 for display — it does not allow switching.
3-When the Q1 symbol is removed from the project, the table shows the correct condition with V1064.0 = 1. 4-If Q1 is absent, again V1064.0 = 1, but why does this happen? Where could the error be?

Connecting Q3 as shown in the right-hand project is correct. Outputs are not meant to be manipulated directly without a proper program connection. Not linking to Q1 in the right-hand project does not follow recommended practices. The inputs/outputs shown in V-memory are read-only and cannot be manually overridden. You might consider setting [product_name] as a slave device. In this mode, it acts merely as a terminal for remote inputs/outputs without containing a program. Would this approach work better for you?
The difference arises because you are working in the simulation, not with a real [product_name] device.

Hello [user_name], Please post your queries in English since this is an international forum. Posting in English will help you get more responses. Here is the translated version of your question. Regards, [user_name]

The VM bit table shows VB1024.0 is set to 1 if the diagram on the right does not include output Q1. This observation contradicts your statement that byte VB1024 is only an image and cannot be written. Additionally, there is an option for Q in the Ethernet output menu. What is your opinion on this?

It seems you are reluctant to accept that you cannot write to this memory area in an actual [product_name] device; only the operating system manages that. You can hold a different view, but do not expect further replies if you persist otherwise.

The variable Q in the network output menu is intended for a Master/Slave connection, not for Master/Master (Client/Server) setups. In Master/Slave mode, one [product_name] acts as master and the other as slave, which must be set to slave mode via Tools > Transfer > Configure Master/Slave mode. The slave [product_name] becomes passive, has no program, and provides hardware to the master, which can then control outputs like Q1 via NQ.
Refer to this application example from [company_name] Building Automation: House Control with [product_name] and Master-Slave Communication ([product_name] Set [article_no]).
You are correct, you cannot input the address V1024 in the internet configuration menu.
[user_name], that’s a helpful suggestion. This means outputs can be controlled when [product_name] acts as a client and does not contain a program.

Why is that? If the second [product_name] is also a client and has no program, how could it function? If using Master/Slave mode, the master controls outputs and reads inputs of the slave [product_name], which remains passive without a program. With Master/Master mode, both devices act as client and server and both have programs.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering inconsistencies between the simulation and actual device behavior in [product_name] when remotely controlling outputs and monitoring their status in V-memory. There is confusion about when V-memory bits truly represent output states and whether these bits are writable. The difference between how simulation handles status updates versus actual devices is leading to misunderstandings about the system's capabilities and operational logic.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the simulation mode to reliably mirror real device behavior. They anticipate that changes to output status and V-memory bits via network control should be instantly reflected and consistent with the logic implemented in their project. Additionally, users presume remote output control and V-memory status should be writable and in alignment with the control flow.
